harbor_p13_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_001.text: Before sunrise in the fifteenth week, the outer mooring chains began to sing. The sound reached Yue through the wall of her room, a long metallic note unlike the clatter she knew from ordinary loading. She dressed without lighting her practice lamp. At the doorway the keeper handed her breakfast wrapped in cloth and said the weather report had worsened overnight. The captain's messenger had come on foot. Yue ate while walking inland to the contact room, where Han already stood beside the shutters with a kettle and a face that looked older than yesterday.

harbor_p13_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_002.text: The harbor master closed the exposed ferry crossing before the first passenger departure. An authorized message launch made its sheltered circuit while the inner channel still met the pilot's limits, taking the warning to the far collection point and returning before closure there too. Twelve copper from the emergency message category covered that contracted circuit. Yue saw the returned pilot's time beside the written warning. Across the water, the appointment keeper had posted a postponement and a receiving address. A woman whose reply was due would be inconvenienced. She would not be sent into dangerous water to preserve a timetable.

harbor_p13_003.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p13_003.text: People will come here because the boats have stopped. Some will be angry at us for stopping them, and some will be afraid to tell us where they were going. We can give the actual closure notice, the next update time and the dry shelter route. We cannot tell them the crossing will reopen tonight. I would rather have somebody swear at a true answer than leave with a comfortable invention. You take the near table this morning. I will cover the doorway, where they can see a person before they see another piece of paper.

harbor_p13_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_004.text: Aning arrived carrying her aunt's delivery list under her coat. The accounting shop had canceled its quay collection, but one customer had already set out from the village. She wanted his name on the contact board if he appeared. Han asked what could be posted publicly and Aning gave only the shop and receiving hour. The customer's family address stayed inside the permitted request. Then she hesitated at the door. Fen usually came down this lane for copying work. Yue said the binder had moved today's task indoors and had confirmed Fen's arrival. Aning let her shoulders fall.

harbor_p13_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_005.text: He Ming's partnership had finished the promised dry packing before the rain. The completed parcels remained on raised boards in their rented shore room, under the agreed storage conditions. An Shou wanted to move them to a cousin's loft because the cousin said it was safer. Zhou Yin asked whether the loft's roof actually held. Nobody knew. He Ming chose the inspected room and asked the owner about the drain instead of following the loudest reassurance. When the first water backed through the yard, their decision would still be tested. A correct choice did not purchase a kind storm.

harbor_p13_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_006.text: Yan found Bo wrestling a stubborn shutter beside the hauling lane. Workers had secured the adjacent opening; this one caught on a bent hook. Bo offered to hold it until somebody found a hammer. The foreman gave him the hammer already on the crew cart and told him where to stand while the other worker braced the leaf. A practical success steadied the young man's hands. Then a gust dragged rain beneath the roof, and the whole cart shook. Bo looked toward the channel with his mouth open. Yan said his name once, quietly, and pointed back to the hinge.

harbor_p13_007.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_p13_007.text: Fear makes you look at the largest thing moving. Our work is the next safe thing within reach. Finish this hook from the sheltered side. Then leave the cart where the roster says and go to the staging room. You are not to follow a loose rope down the lane because you remember its price. A rope can be replaced. If I forget that later, you are allowed to say it to me. Say it loudly enough for the crew to hear. I am giving the permission now while my ears still work.

harbor_p13_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_008.text: At the shelter, Wu carried her youngest child's duck basket with both arms and an expression suggesting the bird had personally designed the weather. Her inland room was still dry, but the neighbor had warned about a loosened chimney cap, and she chose the safer temporary beds rather than wait beneath it. Her older child wanted to know whether this meant another move. She said no: their lease remained theirs, and a room could need checking without becoming lost. He Ming met them at the doorway and took the food parcel, leaving the basket to its indignant owner.

harbor_p13_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_009.text: The shelter keeper assigned spaces from the checked capacity sheet. The repaired corner stayed dry under the first hard rain. An older man refused the bed nearest the wall because he remembered a different building collapsing there decades ago. The keeper could have argued that the wall was sound. Instead she exchanged his place with a willing younger couple and kept the aisle clear. Yue brought a confirmed message from the office on her break and saw how many troubles fit inside the word shelter. A roof held bodies together. It did not make their fears agree.

harbor_p13_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_010.text: Qin arrived at the contact room with the replacement custodian who now covered his ordinary wage duties. The closed guarantee papers remained at their proper office; he carried no chest through the storm. He had brought only the approved public status sheet and his own lunch. Han asked why he had walked in the rain if the task could wait. He said the keeper needed to know he would not attend the canceled meeting. Then he looked embarrassed. His garden had flooded, and sitting alone beside the window had seemed worse than telling somebody a fact they already knew.

harbor_p13_011.speaker: harbor_qin_shuo
harbor_p13_011.text: There is a bed of beans against the back wall. I planted them too early because the ground looked ready. My wife used to tell me I confuse impatience with a favorable season. I remembered that only after the water arrived. I will clear the drain when it is safe and see what survives. Please do not put this on the public damage board yet. A man is permitted to mourn six foolish beans privately. If the shelter needs another pair of ordinary hands, I can wash bowls while doing it.

harbor_p13_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_012.text: By midmorning the weather keeper's revised tide reading reached the room. The expected peak now overlapped the strongest gust interval. The harbor master ordered the low quay cleared and activated the existing shelter, care and extra-shift plan. Sui received the technical assignment for the anchored screen by the narrow inland passage. It would protect that passage from light roof fragments and spray within its rating. The dry evacuation lane ran behind it; ropes and trained crews would control people on the bank. Nobody assigned the screen the task of holding the harbor's rising water outside.

harbor_p13_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_013.text: The first evacuation group came from three low workshops. Wen Zhi walked beside his empty tubs, which remained stacked at his own premises after their earlier return. He had chosen to leave them on a raised platform rather than pay somebody to carry six bulky containers into a crowded shelter. He wore his brother's old scarf and disliked how pleased a neighbor looked to offer help. At the lane entrance he stopped to check that the workshop lock had caught. Yan gave him time to look from the safe side. Then he left, without taking the risk back.

harbor_p13_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_014.text: Deren came from the stock room with its regular supervisor. His current duties allowed careful sorting on dry floors, not wet climbing or emergency bracing. He hated being directed toward a seat while younger workers moved equipment past him. Bo noticed and asked him to read the crew's returned-tool marks from the sheltered table. The ordinary task belonged within Deren's restrictions and mattered to the handover. He accepted it, grumbling that Bo's handwriting had become an injury of its own. The boy grinned. Their friendship found work that did not require pretending an ankle was recovered.

harbor_p13_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_015.text: The first loud crack came from a packing shed roof on the cleared strip. A loosened wooden lath struck the outer stone edging and broke into pieces. The crew stopped passage while Sui checked the wind angle against the screen's working position. Two of the six stored stones were signed out by the designated keeper and seated in the port frame. The remaining four stayed secured. Sui waited for the licensed operator to confirm the anchoring and then authorized a brief activation. Light scattered beneath the passage roof, thin and blue, while ordinary people watched their own footing.

harbor_p13_016.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p13_016.text: Keep the lane behind the frame. This is the tested fragment angle, and we will close passage if it changes. Nobody waits under it to admire the light. Yan, send the next group through in the ordinary order while the crew checks the far corner. Yue, stay at the receiving table and repeat the shelter directions in words. I know you can make a dry marker behave. I am asking for your voice today because I need these people to know where they are going, and because you can do that without spending your strength.

harbor_p13_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_017.text: Yue repeated the directions to a porter holding a small red sewing box. He had rescued it from his room and now seemed unable to hear anything except the possibility of losing it. She asked him to keep the box under his coat while he walked. He obeyed that particular instruction and then heard the next one. Behind him, a woman carrying no possessions turned back toward the quay. Her daughter worked at a laundry inland. Han checked the laundry's confirmed closure message and sent her toward its receiving room, which lay beyond the shelter on the dry road.

harbor_p13_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_018.text: A cart arrived with a man whose shin had been struck by a fallen board. Two trained workers had supported him from the cleared workshop doorway using the ordinary trolley. The care attendant received him, examined the injury and arranged the prescribed treatment. Yue's part was to learn the name he wished sent to his family and pass it to the assigned contact keeper. He asked whether he would lose tomorrow's wage. She said that question would have its own supported answer; right now the attendant needed him to keep his leg still. He swore, then did.

harbor_p13_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_019.text: The screen took the small fragments it was rated to divert. It made a sound like grit sliding down a bowl. Beyond its narrow coverage, a larger roof plank fell harmlessly into the cleared water. Yue felt the old impulse to reach for another arm and catch what she saw moving. The distance, weight and wet footing made the impulse useless. She kept both hands on the receiving table until it passed. Later she would remember the choice as less dramatic than the falling plank and more difficult than she wanted to admit to anybody.

harbor_p13_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_020.text: At the far end of the lane, Yan heard a mooring line fail. A small repair skiff swung against its neighboring berth with two yard workers still aboard. The harbor master had ordered vessels cleared, and their supervisor believed they had already left. They had returned for a tool bag after the head count, without telling the receiving crew. Now the bow remained near the bank while the stern pulled outward. Yan stopped the lane and called the trained bank crew to the marked position. The workers crouched where the pilot directed them, abandoning the bag.

harbor_p13_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_021.text: The ordinary recovery line reached the nearer worker on the second throw. Its first loop had blown aside, and he had almost lunged after it. The pilot shouted for him to wait. One crew member held the line from the protected bank position while another controlled the skiff's existing bow lead from the bollard. Yan stayed clear of the load path and directed the transfer to the low landing step. Nobody tied a line around Yue or asked her qi arms to become an anchor. The first worker moved ashore shaking so badly he could not apologize.

harbor_p13_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_022.text: The second worker had slipped between the bench and a folded sail. Her sleeve caught, and for a moment she seemed to be holding herself back. Bo reached for a knife from the crew kit only after the pilot asked for it. The worker cut the trapped cloth where she could safely reach and crawled toward the bow. Yue heard the rip from the table. It sounded indecently small against the wind. The bank crew helped her onto the step before the skiff's stern struck the piling again. The two workers were received together, then examined separately.

harbor_p13_023.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_p13_023.text: We have both workers ashore. Leave the skiff. The bow line is not a promise that we can save somebody's property next. Move back behind the lane boundary now, including anybody who came here to watch. Bo, hand the kit to its keeper and take the receiving count to the shelter. Tell them two people, with the names the attendant confirms. Do not send a tale about a vanished boat ahead of them. Their families need to know what happened, and these two need care before the whole harbor decides who they are.

harbor_p13_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_024.text: The older worker wept over the abandoned bag after her breathing steadied. It held ordinary tools she had bought over years. The younger man kept saying he had told her not to return, although he had returned with her. Sui took their account through the receiving clerk without asking for a confession while they shivered. The supervisor's count would need correction, and the return after clearance would need review. None of that required denying blankets. Yue placed a cup of water within the older woman's reach and waited while she chose whether to take it.

harbor_p13_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_025.text: Outside, the screen's two stones dimmed after their logged interval. The operator closed the passage while the ordinary crew checked that the latest roof debris had stopped. Both stones were exhausted and marked spent. Four unused stones remained in the locked store; no replacement was silently fitted. The wind angle had shifted beyond the frame's approved coverage, so Sui kept that lane closed and directed the remaining evacuees to the longer inland route. People complained about the distance. The shelter sent a wheeled chair and attendants for the two people who could not manage it unaided.

harbor_p13_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_026.text: He Ming had gone to the shelter intending to help Wu with the children and found Zhou Yin waiting at the door. Water was reaching the rented packing room's threshold, and An Shou wanted one more attempt to raise the lowest board. The merchant's parcels were finished, but the stored wrapping belonged to the partners. He Ming looked down the lane toward their room. Then Wu's youngest child caught her sleeve and asked whether the duck would drown indoors. She said no, and heard herself sound certain about the one thing she could actually see.

harbor_p13_027.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p13_027.text: Tell An Shou to come here by the dry road. We used the agreed room and did the drain check. We can describe the water afterward. I am not going to send him back because six copper in paper feels heavier when it is ours. If the owner opens the door from the safe side later, we can look with him. Until then the parcels remain where they are. You can be angry with me about it. I am frightened too. I would rather have the argument at this doorway than have nobody left to answer it.

harbor_p13_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_028.text: Zhou Yin swore at her, then went to fetch An Shou by the safe route. Wu told the children to stop listening so fiercely to adult quarrels. They listened harder. He Ming sat down beside the basket and discovered she was trembling. The duck shifted within its wicker walls, offended by being placed near a crying woman. Wu covered He Ming's hand with her own. She did not say the goods would be dry. She said they could all eat something when the next pot was ready. That was enough to let He Ming keep sitting.

harbor_p13_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_029.text: At noon Han found the contact room crowded with people who had waited through the rain for an answer. A postponed boat appointment, a missing worker and a household moved to the shelter had become one rumor about a vessel sinking. She wrote three separate confirmed statuses on the board and spoke them aloud. The missing worker had not yet been found. The two rescued yard workers were ashore. The closed ferry had carried no passengers into the exposed channel. A man accused her of hiding the rest. She asked which person he wanted to locate and began there.

harbor_p13_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_030.text: The man wanted a brother who swept the night fish market. He had heard nothing since dawn and had come to the quay because the market lay beyond it. Han called the assigned inland runner, who had already collected a closure sheet from that district. The brother's name was on the staffed refuge list, with permission to tell his household where he waited. The man read it twice. Then he apologized for shouting as if Han had personally arranged the wind. She accepted the apology and asked him to leave the doorway clear for the next person.

harbor_p13_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_031.text: The genuinely unlocated worker was a kitchen porter called Niu. His employer's old roster gave the room he had left last month. The current receiving sheet had no reply from the new address yet. Yue sent the discrepancy to the contact keeper and wrote the last confirmed sighting with its source. She did not add a guessed route across the flooded strip. At the next update a runner reported the inland baker had taken Niu and two neighbors into a dry rear room. Niu had permission to send his new address to his sister, and the message finally reached her.

harbor_p13_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_032.text: Han turned away after the sister thanked her. Yue found her in the back room pressing a damp cloth against her eyes. The clerk said she had imagined Niu in the water every time somebody asked the question. A true missing status had still frightened her, and she resented how composed she had sounded saying it. Yue did not tell her composure was a virtue. She poured tea and sat beside her until the next shift keeper arrived. Outside, the rumor changed into a story of a clerk who knew where everybody was. They both disliked that version.

harbor_p13_033.speaker: harbor_han_pei
harbor_p13_033.text: I wish knowing a name made finding its owner easier. I wish I had not felt relieved about one person while somebody else was waiting for a leg to stop bleeding. That sounds ugly when I say it. At the table it all becomes sensible because the next question needs an answer. Here I am tired and jealous of the person who gets to cry. Please keep the kettle near me for another minute. Then I will hand over properly, and I would like you to walk me to the shelter before I go home.

harbor_p13_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_034.text: Yue's morning contact half-day ended with a handover to the assigned replacement. Han's own roster also permitted relief. They walked inland during the brief interval the route keeper judged passable, stopping behind the ordinary road boundary when a loose sign swung overhead. A worker lowered it from the sheltered side after clearing the space. Nobody asked Yue to hold the sign with qi. Han laughed weakly at how often today had required waiting for someone else's safe task. At the shelter entrance she found Qin washing bowls, his rolled sleeves showing thin, freckled wrists.

harbor_p13_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_035.text: Qin had broken one bowl by gripping it too tightly. The keeper counted it among the ordinary shelter losses and gave him a cloth to hold the next one. He looked more mortified than the error deserved. Deren, seated at the dry receiving table, told him that Bo had already lost a pencil inside his own sleeve and spent ten minutes accusing the floor. Qin smiled and kept washing. Yue realized the shelter's relief came partly from these small ridiculous things. People could still mishandle bowls and pencils while the sea behaved badly, and survive being seen doing so.

harbor_p13_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_036.text: The inn's reserved emergency room opened when the shelter's checked beds filled. Its keeper received the overflow group under the activated agreement, with the nightly charge recorded against the shelter category. A couple tried to reserve their place for an absent nephew. The keeper could hold only a short receiving interval before another person needed it. Han explained the alternative contact route, and they agreed to send him there if he arrived later. The beds were warm ordinary beds. Their warmth depended on people making decisions that would feel unkind if nobody explained the next available place.

harbor_p13_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_037.text: Sui arrived at dusk with salt dried beneath her collar. A falling splinter had cut her cheek outside the cleared lane while she moved between assigned posts. The attendant cleaned the shallow wound and told her to sit until the dressing held. She argued about the handover, then saw Yan carrying the completed sheet to the replacement captain. The job had another competent pair of hands. Her own hands closed uselessly around the chair's edge. Yue offered the supper bowl without making a lesson of it. Sui ate, and the first mouthful seemed to make her angry.

harbor_p13_038.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p13_038.text: My son says I tell people to rest as if I invented the idea. He is right about that. When I sit still, I can hear every decision I might have made sooner. I thought the workshop clearance count was complete. The supervisor thought so too, and two workers returned without telling him. We need to understand that sequence. Tonight they are breathing, and I am grateful. Gratitude does not stop my mind making another version where the rope misses. I would like this soup hotter. That is a complaint I can usefully make now.

harbor_p13_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_039.text: He Ming shared a bench with the rescued tool owner, whose name was Ke Chun. Ke asked whether the cooperative could use somebody who knew canvas stitching. He Ming said their present contracts supported only the existing workers, but she would remember the skill and tell her if a real offer emerged. Ke's expression fell, then steadied. She had not asked for charity; she had wanted a way to replace the tools without waiting for judgment. He Ming described the ordinary work board instead, and Ke asked for its inland location. They spoke as workers with possible futures.

harbor_p13_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_040.text: Zhou Yin returned with An Shou before dark. Both were wet, both angry, and neither had entered the packing room again. An sat beside He Ming and said the threshold water was not yet inside when he left. She thanked him for coming. Zhou wanted the partners to write down whose decision had stopped the last attempt, in case the parcels were damaged. He Ming agreed her own choice should be described. She also wanted the observed water level and the safe-route closure beside it. Their disagreement acquired facts without becoming a friendship that would never disagree again.

harbor_p13_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_041.text: Wu's older child offered An Shou a corner of the toy boat's cloth cover. He used it to dry his fingers until Wu gently explained it belonged to a boat smaller than his thumb. The child insisted the boat had weathered worse storms in the washbasin. An said he respected its service record. Zhou began to laugh and could not stop. He Ming joined her, then cried unexpectedly in the middle of the laughter. Nobody tried to decide which emotion was the correct account of the day. The child looked satisfied that the cloth had been useful.

harbor_p13_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_042.text: Night brought the peak tide against the shore wall. The shelter shook at a gust but held under its completed checks. From an upper window Yue could see no channel lights except the fixed harbor marker. Its ordinary maintenance flame seemed absurdly small beside all that darkness. The keeper closed the shutter and asked people to save the view for daylight. Yue returned to her assigned sleeping place with her habitual pack tucked beneath it. Her cup was already washed. Her pendant remained wrapped. There was no private instrument in the room that could bargain with the water outside.

harbor_p13_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_043.text: Near midnight a child developed a cough that worried her mother. The care attendant examined her in the warmed receiving corner and arranged the appropriate ordinary observation. Another parent tried to offer an unfamiliar herb from a pocket. The attendant asked its source and declined to give it without knowing what it was. Sui, awake on the next bench, helped the mother move the blanket as instructed. The captain's hands were gentle with cloth. Yue saw the care continue through ordinary questions and felt how much she wanted an answer that would make every frightened parent sleep.

harbor_p13_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_044.text: Dai Min sat up sewing a loose button onto the shirt she had worn to the shelter. The keeper had asked for lamps to be put out except at the care corner, so she worked there by invitation while the attendant watched the child. Yue sat nearby. Dai said her husband used to sleep through any storm until somebody mentioned his boat. The memory made her smile, then look toward the closed shutter. She had no boat to worry about now. Her grief found a new shape in that freedom, and she disliked being asked whether it was comforting.

harbor_p13_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_045.text: Yue said nothing about comfort. Dai finished the button and asked whether she could borrow Yue's familiar cup for water. It was an ordinary personal loan made between two women on a shelter bench. The cup came back warm from her hands. Yue had carried it through forests and roads, but this exchange made it feel more like an object from a home. She was surprised by the ache that followed. A person could stay for months and still have a departure somewhere ahead. Dai noticed her face and asked only whether she wanted another blanket.

harbor_p13_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_046.text: At dawn the wind eased enough for the harbor master's observers to inspect from the permitted road. The low quay remained closed until the water receded and ordinary structural checks were complete. People at the shelter wanted to leave immediately. The keeper posted the next actual review time and named the neighborhoods already cleared for return. Wu's inland block needed a chimney inspection first. Wen's workshop lane waited on debris removal. The captain could not clear buildings through affection. He Ming folded a blanket while looking at the clock, furious at the usefulness of waiting.

harbor_p13_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_047.text: The young skiff worker offered to help clear debris before the attendant had finished checking his bruised shoulder. Yan directed him to the rest bench and promised a work decision after the care restriction was known. The man said everybody would call him the fool who went back. Yan said he might hear that, and it would not repair a roof or make his shoulder usable. Bo sat beside him without being asked. For once the young rigger supplied no joke. They watched an ordinary crew carry wet boards past the shelter window and let silence do its work.

harbor_p13_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_048.text: The packing room opened under the owner's supervision after the safe approach was restored. He Ming and Zhou attended; An stayed at the shelter until his dry clothes arrived. Water had entered one corner and soaked the partners' spare wrapping. The completed merchant parcels stood dry on the raised boards. A lower sack of their own rough cord had taken damp but could be separated for assessment. He Ming touched the ruined paper and felt Zhou watching. Their decision had preserved people and most of the work. It had not preserved everything they owned, which made the praise feel premature.

harbor_p13_049.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p13_049.text: The finished parcels are dry. We will tell the merchant what we saw and let the agreed inspection happen. Our paper loss belongs in our own account until we know whether the room's drain failed beyond the conditions we were promised. I chose not to send An back. I will not change that sentence because the paper is wet. I also will not tell you this is a good morning. I wanted to make something that survived ordinary trade. Now I would like an hour to be angry before we decide how to buy wrapping again.

harbor_p13_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_050.text: Zhou said she wanted the same hour. They locked the room and went to the tea stall, which had reopened inland with boiled water and an abbreviated menu. The owner asked whether they wanted the sweet buns usually kept for visitors. He Ming said she was now sufficiently offended by the sea to count as a visitor to her own town. They bought two buns with private money and argued about which had more filling. Yue passed the doorway carrying a contact packet and saw them laughing. She did not stop to turn their laughter into evidence of recovery.

harbor_p13_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_051.text: The emergency keeper collected the first checked invoices after the immediate receiving work settled. Shelter, care and meals had cost forty: twenty for meals, twelve for the activated overflow beds, eight for prescribed immediate care supplies and attendance. Equipment and ordinary temporary bracing cost twelve: eight for braces and four for replacement rope. Nine authorized extra half-shifts at two copper made eighteen. The warning circuit had cost twelve before closure. These eighty-two joined the earlier sixteen stone purchase, making ninety-eight spent from two hundred forty. The unspent balance was one hundred forty-two, with four unused stones held separately.

harbor_p13_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_052.text: The category balances stayed visible without asking storm victims to memorize them. Fifty-six remained for shelter and care, thirty-two for equipment, thirty for extra shifts and twenty-four for message boats. Nobody called the four stones extra copper. The exhausted drill pair and storm pair could not be used again. Commercial parcel losses had no automatic claim on this reserve, and later injury or property awards would require their own proper sources. Sui read the account once, asked the keeper to retain the purchase and use records, and went outside to hear the ordinary workers' accounts of the skiff return.

harbor_p13_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_053.text: Yue's two scheduled half-days that week were the storm morning contact desk and the following dry-room return-status work. She received four copper for them, while six paid the week's agreed bed and meals. Her new term had spent forty-four in total and retained one hundred fifty-six within its lines. The safety reserve paid no extra wage to her. When Han offered to write a note thanking her for staying nearby through the difficult evening, Yue accepted the thanks as a friend's words. The term had a roster, and friendship had an evening beside a borrowed bowl.

harbor_p13_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_054.text: Fen arrived at the reopened contact room with a bundle from the binder and her father walking carefully behind her. Their lodgings had stayed dry. Luo had lost a day's sorting while the owner closed the shop, under the ordinary wage terms that now needed checking. Fen wanted to tell Han all this, then stopped when she saw the clerk's face. She asked whether Han had slept. Han said a little. Fen put the bundle down and fetched water before asking for the next copying task. Her father's smile held both pride and the sadness of needing less.

harbor_p13_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_055.text: Aning appeared at the door with two sweet buns her aunt had bought for the shop staff. One belonged to Fen by the aunt's invitation, which Aning explained because she feared somebody would turn the gift into another debt. Fen took it and asked whether the bun came with an account column. Aning said the filling probably did. They ate on the back step while Yue sorted the permitted public statuses inside. Their conversation drifted from the storm to an apprenticeship vacancy inland. Fen listened without deciding. The storm had interrupted a young woman's plans; it had not replaced them.

harbor_p13_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_056.text: Sui inspected the empty passage after the screen had cooled and the crew had checked it. A roof fragment rested beyond the protected strip. She picked it up only after the site keeper cleared the area. Its weight was less than she expected, its sharp edge more dangerous. Yue joined her outside the closed frame. The captain asked what she had found hardest. Yue told her about wanting to catch the larger falling plank. Sui looked at the fragment and said she understood the temptation. They left it with the incident keeper, where an object could support a fact.

harbor_p13_057.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p13_057.text: I am glad you told me. A person can obey the safe plan and still be ashamed of the thing she imagined doing instead. My imagined mistake was letting the passage stay open after the angle changed, because the longer road angered people. I closed it, and I keep hearing their complaints as if they were evidence I failed. They are evidence the road was longer. We can examine whether a better route is possible afterward. Today I would like us both to sleep before trying to improve the entire shore.

harbor_p13_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_058.text: Yan went home only after the replacement foreman accepted the returned crew count and tools. His mother had left soup warming under a cover and a note asking him to bring no wet boots into the room. He obeyed the second instruction before reading the first again. Bo's permission to contradict him had worked once during the night: the boy told him to leave a dragging coil where it lay. Yan felt embarrassed and grateful. He cleaned the boots on the doorstep, then ate soup whose ordinary flavor reached him through exhaustion more strongly than any praise.

harbor_p13_059.speaker: narrator
harbor_p13_059.text: Yue closed her personal notes at the end of the fifteenth week with the storm still audible in remembered intervals. She wrote the four remaining stones, the actual balances and the names she had permission to keep privately. Then she wrote a sentence about Han crying beside the kettle and left the names out of that one. Official accounts would explain where help went and what failed. Her own notes could remember the silence between friends. Outside, a neighbor hammered a shutter latch back into place. The next week would begin with watermarks on walls and people wanting answers.
